newsitem.title: USA: Overwhelming Senate vote for Albright predicted.
newsitem.headline: Overwhelming Senate vote for Albright predicted.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott predicted on Tuesday that Madeleine Albright would be overwhelmingly confirmed by the Senate on Wednesday as the first female U.S. Secretary of State.
"I think the vote will be overwhelming, if not unanimous," Lott, a Mississippi Republican, said at a news conference.

Albright, currently U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, was approved 18-0 by the Senate Foreign Relations Committee on Monday to succeed Warren Christopher. His resignation took effect on Monday as President Bill Clinton was being sworn in for his second term.
If confirmed as expected, Albright likely would be sworn in on Thursday.
U.S. officials said Albright was considering making her first overseas trip from Feb. 12-22, travelling to world capitals in Europe and Asia.
Albright, 59, was born in Prague and emmigrated to the United States with her family at the age of 11, fleeing Nazism and communism after the Second World War.

Before being named to the U.N., she taught international relations at Georgetown University, headed a Democratic Party think tank and advised unsuccessful Democratic presidential contenders Walter Mondale and Michael Dukakis. She also worked for ex President Jimmy Carter and former Sen. Edmund Muskie.
